chapter_summary: The night before Jesus died, He did something shocking: He got up from the table, wrapped a towel around Himself, and washed His disciples' dirty feet — a job only servants did. Then He gave His followers a new commandment: love one another the way He had loved them. He also told them that Judas would betray Him, and that Peter would deny Him three times before the rooster crowed.
main_lesson: Jesus showed us that true greatness is serving others. He is the Lord of all — and He chose to wash feet. His new commandment is simple: love one another the way Jesus loves us.

memory_verse.kjv: A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.
memory_verse.little_bible: Jesus gave a new command: love each other the same way I have loved you.

parent_guide: John 13 opens the 'Upper Room Discourse' — five chapters where Jesus prepares His disciples for His death. Three moments anchor the chapter: (1) The foot-washing (vv1-17) — Jesus, knowing He was God, chose the posture of a slave. This is not merely a lesson in humility; it is a picture of the cross itself, where the Holy One stoops to cleanse the unclean. (2) The betrayal of Judas (vv18-30) — Jesus was not surprised. He identified Judas and released him, showing that even betrayal is within God's sovereign plan. (3) The new commandment (vv31-38) — 'Love one another as I have loved you' is the defining mark of a Christian. Not doctrine alone, not rituals alone — love. Help your children understand that this love is not a feeling but a choice to serve.
application_for_children: Jesus is the most important person who ever lived — and He chose to wash dirty feet. That means you can serve others too, even when it feels hard. And when you love people the way Jesus loves you — kindly, patiently, generously — everyone will know you belong to Jesus.

verses.kjv: Now before the feast of the passover, when Jesus knew that his hour was come that he should depart out of this world unto the Father, having loved his own which were in the world, he loved them unto the end.
verses.little_bible: Before the Passover feast, Jesus knew His time had come. He was leaving this world to go back to the Father. He had always loved His followers — and He loved them to the very end.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: It was almost time for Jesus to leave the world. He loved His friends completely — all the way to the end.
verses.meaning: John opens this chapter with the most important thing: Jesus knew what was coming, and He chose to love anyway. His love for us did not shrink at the cross — it was fully shown there.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for loving me all the way to the end.
verses.discussion_question: Can you love someone even when things are hard?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus knew He was going to die, and He still chose to love His friends completely. What does that tell us about the kind of love Jesus has for us?
verses.do_it_today: Tell someone in your family that you love them — and mean it with your whole heart.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus sitting at a long table with His disciples in a warm upper room, oil lamps glowing, the disciples talking together, Jesus gazing at them with deep, tender love on His face. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: And supper being ended, the devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon's son, to betray him;
verses.little_bible: While they were eating supper, the devil put a wicked plan into Judas's heart. Judas was going to hand Jesus over to His enemies.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Judas had a bad plan in his heart. The devil put it there.
verses.meaning: Even at the table of love, evil was at work. Judas sat with Jesus and still chose betrayal. This shows that being near Jesus is not enough — our hearts must truly follow Him.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, keep my heart close to You and far from evil.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it important to have good thoughts in our heart?
verses.family_discussion: Judas was with Jesus but his heart turned away. How can we make sure our hearts stay close to Jesus each day?
verses.do_it_today: Ask Jesus to fill your heart with good things today — and say no to anything bad that tries to sneak in.
verses.illustration_prompt: A long table with a shared meal, one disciple at the far end with a shadowed, troubled expression, the other disciples eating and talking in warm lamplight. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Jesus knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he was come from God, and went to God;
verses.little_bible: Jesus knew who He was. The Father had put everything in His hands. He had come from God — and He was going back to God.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus knew He came from God. He knew God gave Him all power.
verses.meaning: Jesus served from a place of security and strength, not weakness. He washed feet because He knew He was Lord — not because He was trying to prove anything. True humility comes from knowing who you are in God.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are all-powerful and You still chose to serve.
verses.discussion_question: Is it easier to be kind when you feel safe and loved?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus served others because He was secure in who He was. How does knowing God loves us help us serve others without needing praise?
verses.do_it_today: Do one act of service today without telling anyone or expecting a thank-you.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus standing quietly by the table, eyes closed for a moment in prayer, a calm and certain expression, light streaming from above, disciples unaware around Him. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: He riseth from supper, and laid aside his garments; and took a towel, and girded himself.
verses.little_bible: Jesus got up from the meal. He took off His outer robe. He picked up a towel and wrapped it around Himself like a servant.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus got up and wrapped a towel around Himself like a servant.
verses.meaning: Jesus chose to act like a servant. He did not wait for someone else to do it. He stood up and prepared to serve. This is what love looks like — it moves, it acts, it serves.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me get up and serve others like You did.
verses.discussion_question: What does a servant do that makes them different from a boss?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus is King of kings — yet He wrapped Himself in a towel. What does this teach us about what true greatness looks like?
verses.do_it_today: Do a chore or job at home that someone else usually does — cheerfully and without being asked.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus standing and wrapping a long white towel around His waist, outer robe set aside on the bench, the disciples watching in surprise, warm lamplight filling the room. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: After that he poureth water into a bason, and began to wash the disciples' feet, and to wipe them with the towel wherewith he was girded.
verses.little_bible: Jesus poured water into a big bowl. Then He knelt down and began washing His disciples' feet. He dried them with the towel He wore.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus poured water in a bowl. He washed His disciples' dirty feet.
verses.meaning: Washing feet was the job of the lowest servant. Roads were dusty and feet were dirty. Jesus chose to do what no one else wanted to do — a picture of how He would soon wash away our sins.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, You cleaned dirty feet. You can clean my heart too.
verses.discussion_question: Would you wash someone else's dirty feet? Why or why not?
verses.family_discussion: Washing feet was considered a very humble job. Why do you think Jesus chose to do it Himself? What was He teaching His disciples?
verses.do_it_today: Help clean something at home that is usually messy — without complaining.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus kneeling on the stone floor, gently holding the foot of a disciple over a clay basin of water, tender focus on His face, other disciples watching with wide eyes. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Then cometh he to Simon Peter: and Peter saith unto him, Lord, dost thou wash my feet?
verses.little_bible: Jesus came to Simon Peter. Peter was shocked. He said: 'Lord — are You going to wash MY feet?'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus came to Peter. Peter was shocked: 'Lord, are You washing my feet?'
verses.meaning: Peter could not believe it. The idea of Jesus — his Lord and Teacher — washing his feet felt completely wrong to him. Sometimes we resist God's grace because it feels too humbling to receive.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me receive Your love even when it surprises me.
verses.discussion_question: Was Peter right to be surprised? Why do you think he felt that way?
verses.family_discussion: Peter was shocked that Jesus would serve him. Has God's love or kindness ever surprised you in a big way?
verses.do_it_today: Tell someone a way that God or a friend surprised you with kindness — and thank them for it.
verses.illustration_prompt: Peter sitting with his foot lifted in surprise, mouth open, looking up at Jesus kneeling before him with the basin of water, the other disciples watching, warm lamp glow. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Jesus answered and said unto him, What I do thou knowest not now; but thou shalt know hereafter.
verses.little_bible: Jesus answered him: 'You do not understand what I am doing right now. But you will understand later.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'You don't understand yet. You will understand later.'
verses.meaning: Jesus did not always explain everything in the moment. He asked Peter to trust Him. God often works in ways we don't understand at first — but He promises understanding will come.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me trust You even when I don't understand.
verses.discussion_question: Have you ever not understood something until later? What happened?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus told Peter he would understand later. Can you think of a time when something hard made sense later on?
verses.do_it_today: When something confuses you today, say: 'Jesus, I trust You even though I don't understand.'
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus looking up calmly at Peter with gentle, knowing eyes, Peter's expression still puzzled, the basin of water between them, warm firelight in the room. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Peter saith unto him, Thou shalt never wash my feet. Jesus answered him, If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me.
verses.little_bible: Peter said: 'You will NEVER wash my feet!' Jesus answered: 'If I do not wash you, you cannot belong to Me.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Peter said: 'Never!' Jesus said: 'Then you cannot be part of Me.'
verses.meaning: Peter's refusal was well-meant but wrong. To be part of Jesus, we must let Him cleanse us — of sin, of pride, of everything. We cannot stay with Jesus while refusing His grace.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, I need Your cleansing. Wash me clean.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it hard sometimes to let others help us?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus said Peter could not belong to Him without being washed. What do you think He meant by that — both physically and spiritually?
verses.do_it_today: Pray and ask Jesus to forgive any wrong thing you did this week. Let Him wash you clean.
verses.illustration_prompt: Peter's arms crossed stubbornly, Jesus looking at him with serious but loving eyes, the basin of water waiting, tension between the two figures, warm lamp behind them. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Simon Peter saith unto him, Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and my head.
verses.little_bible: Then Peter swung the other way. He said: 'Lord, then wash not just my feet — wash my hands and my head too!'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Peter said: 'Then wash my hands and head too, Lord!'
verses.meaning: Peter went from total refusal to wanting everything at once. This is Peter's passionate heart — all or nothing. God meets us in our eagerness, but teaches us that His grace is already enough.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, wash all of me — I belong completely to You.
verses.discussion_question: Do you ever go from saying no to wanting everything all at once?
verses.family_discussion: Peter jumped from 'never' to 'all of me!' What does this tell us about how we should come to Jesus — holding back or fully open?
verses.do_it_today: Give Jesus one thing today you have been holding back from Him — a worry, a habit, a dream.
verses.illustration_prompt: Peter leaning forward eagerly with his hands stretched out toward Jesus, wide enthusiastic eyes, Jesus smiling gently, the basin between them. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Jesus saith to him, He that is washed needeth not save to wash his feet, but is clean every whit: and ye are clean, but not all.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'If you have already bathed, you only need your feet washed. You are clean — not your whole body again. You disciples are clean.' But He added: 'Not all of you.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'You are clean. But not everyone here is clean.'
verses.meaning: Those who belong to Jesus have been fully cleansed — they don't need to start over. But daily following means daily humility. Jesus also hints that one among them was not truly clean — Judas.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You that Your forgiveness makes me completely clean.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to be clean on the inside, not just outside?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus said His disciples were clean — meaning forgiven and belonging to Him. What does it mean to you that Jesus has made you clean?
verses.do_it_today: Write down one thing Jesus has forgiven you for and thank Him for making you clean.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus gesturing toward the disciples with a kind but serious expression, the washed feet of several disciples visible, one figure (Judas) in shadow at the edge. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: For he knew who should betray him; therefore said he, Ye are not all clean.
verses.little_bible: Jesus already knew who would betray Him. That is why He said: 'Not all of you are clean.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus knew who would betray Him. That is why He said not all were clean.
verses.meaning: Jesus knew Judas's heart — and He still served him. He still washed his feet. This is a picture of God's patience with people who have not yet turned to Him.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, You know my heart. Keep it pure and true to You.
verses.discussion_question: Does it feel different knowing Jesus knows everything about us?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus knew Judas would betray Him and still washed his feet. What does that tell us about how God treats people who haven't yet turned to Him?
verses.do_it_today: Be kind today to someone who has been unkind to you — just like Jesus was to Judas.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus glancing toward one shadowed disciple with knowing sadness in His eyes, the rest of the disciples unaware, the basin and towel still in view. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: So after he had washed their feet, and had taken his garments, and was set down again, he said unto them, Know ye what I have done to you?
verses.little_bible: When Jesus had finished washing all their feet, He put His robe back on and sat down again. He asked them: 'Do you understand what I have done for you?'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus sat back down and asked: 'Do you know what I just did for you?'
verses.meaning: Jesus did not leave the lesson unspoken. He asked them to think about it. We should always ask: 'What is Jesus teaching me through this?'
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me understand the lessons You teach me.
verses.discussion_question: What do you think Jesus was trying to teach His disciples by washing their feet?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus finished serving and then asked a question. How does stopping to think about what God has done help us grow?
verses.do_it_today: After you help someone today, ask yourself: 'Why did I do that, and what did I learn?'
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus sitting at the head of the table again, robe back on, leaning forward to ask the disciples a question, the disciples listening carefully, the basin of water set to one side. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Ye call me Master and Lord: and ye say well; for so I am.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'You call Me Teacher and Lord — and you are right. That is who I am.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'You call Me Lord and Teacher. You are right — I am!'
verses.meaning: Jesus was not falsely humble. He confirmed He truly is Lord and Teacher. The foot-washing was not a denial of His lordship — it was a demonstration of what lordship truly looks like.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are my Lord. I want to follow You.
verses.discussion_question: What makes someone a good teacher or a good leader?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus said 'I am Lord and Teacher' — and then He washed feet. What kind of leader does that show He is?
verses.do_it_today: Think about what it means to call Jesus 'Lord' in your life. Is there something He is asking you to change?
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus seated at the table, speaking with calm authority, disciples leaning in to listen, warm golden light from oil lamps, an expression of quiet confidence on His face. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet; ye also ought to wash one another's feet.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'I am your Lord and Teacher — and I washed your feet. So you should wash each other's feet too.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'I washed your feet. Now you should wash each other's feet too.'
verses.meaning: Jesus sets the pattern: if the greatest serves, then all who follow Him must serve. Serving one another is not optional for Christians — it is a direct command from Jesus.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me serve others the way You served me.
verses.discussion_question: Who can you serve at home or at school this week?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus told His disciples to wash one another's feet. What are some everyday ways your family can serve each other?
verses.do_it_today: Serve one person in your home today — do something for them before they even ask.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus pointing to the disciples around the table, gesturing as He teaches, the disciples nodding and listening, the empty basin visible in the corner of the room. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: For I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'I have shown you how to live. Do the same things I did.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'I showed you the way. Now do it too.'
verses.meaning: Jesus did not just teach with words — He showed the way with actions. He is our example in everything: in serving, in loving, in giving, in trusting God.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, let my life look more and more like Yours.
verses.discussion_question: Who is a good example in your life? How do they help you?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus is our ultimate example. In what area of your life do you most want to copy what Jesus did?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one thing Jesus did — and do that same thing for someone today.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus standing, arms open, the disciples surrounding Him, an expression of loving invitation on His face, warm lamplight, the washed feet of the disciples visible. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Verily, verily, I say unto you, The servant is not greater than his lord; neither he that is sent greater than he that sent him.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'A servant is not greater than his master. A messenger is not greater than the one who sent him.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'A servant is never greater than the master.'
verses.meaning: If Jesus — who is the greatest — chose to serve, then no follower of Jesus can claim to be too important to serve. Serving is always right and always good.
verses.memory_phrase: No one is too great to serve.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, remind me that I am here to serve, not to be served.
verses.discussion_question: Is it ever right to think you are too important to help someone?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus said that no servant is greater than their master. How does this truth shape the way we treat others — especially people who need help?
verses.do_it_today: Help with a task today that feels 'below' you — and do it gladly.
verses.illustration_prompt: A small servant figure beside a larger master figure, then Jesus between them pointing to both, the disciples seated around the table listening, warm and teaching atmosphere. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: If ye know these things, happy are ye if ye do them.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'You will be happy and blessed if you know these things AND do them.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'If you know this and do it, you will be truly happy.'
verses.meaning: Knowing is not enough — doing is what brings blessing. God's Word is not for information; it is for transformation. The blessed life comes from obeying, not just knowing.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me not just know but also do what You teach.
verses.discussion_question: What is the difference between knowing something and actually doing it?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus says happiness comes from doing His teaching, not just hearing it. Is there a teaching from the Bible your family knows but hasn't yet put into practice?
verses.do_it_today: Pick one thing Jesus has taught you and actually do it today — on purpose.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus smiling warmly at the disciples, pointing outward as if sending them into the world, soft golden light around Him, the disciples looking encouraged. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: I speak not of you all: I know whom I have chosen: but that the scripture may be fulfilled, He that eateth bread with me hath lifted up his heel against me.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'I am not talking about all of you. I know the ones I chose. But the Scripture must come true: even someone who shared My food will turn against Me.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'I know who I chose. The Bible said someone close to Me would betray Me.'
verses.meaning: The betrayal of Jesus was not an accident or a surprise to God. It was foretold in Scripture (Psalm 41:9). Even the darkest moment in history was within God's plan.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, I trust that Your plan is always perfect.
verses.discussion_question: Does it comfort you knowing that God knew everything before it happened?
verses.family_discussion: The Bible predicted that Jesus would be betrayed — and it happened exactly that way. What does that tell us about how trustworthy the Bible is?
verses.do_it_today: Read one promise from the Bible today and choose to trust that God will keep it.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus gesturing toward a scroll as He speaks, the disciples listening with serious expressions, one disciple (Judas) sitting slightly apart, evening lamplight. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Now I tell you before it come, that, when it is come to pass, ye may believe that I am he.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'I am telling you what will happen before it happens. When it comes true, you will know that I am who I say I am.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'I am telling you ahead of time so you will believe Me.'
verses.meaning: Jesus predicted the future so that when it happened exactly as He said, faith would grow. God tells us what will happen in advance because He wants us to trust Him completely.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, I believe You are who You say You are.
verses.discussion_question: If someone told you something before it happened and it came true, would you trust them more?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus told His disciples ahead of time so they would believe. How does reading Bible prophecies that came true help your faith grow?
verses.do_it_today: Find one prophecy Jesus made in the Gospels that came true — and share it with someone.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus speaking with steady, calm certainty, His hands open, a knowing peace on His face, the disciples listening with a mixture of wonder and unease. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that receiveth whomsoever I send receiveth me; and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'Whoever welcomes the one I send is welcoming Me. And whoever welcomes Me is welcoming God who sent Me.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'Welcoming My messengers is welcoming Me — and welcoming God.'
verses.meaning: There is a chain of honour: God → Jesus → those Jesus sends. To welcome a servant of Jesus is to welcome Jesus Himself. This gives dignity and purpose to all who serve in Jesus's name.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me welcome the people You send into my life.
verses.discussion_question: How do you treat people who come to tell you about Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus said welcoming His messengers is welcoming God. How does that change the way we treat pastors, missionaries, and anyone who shares the Gospel?
verses.do_it_today: Welcome someone new to your church, school, or neighbourhood with kindness this week.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus gesturing outward with both hands as if sending the disciples out, a chain of figures reaching from God in heaven to Jesus to the disciples, warm golden scene. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: When Jesus had thus said, he was troubled in spirit, and testified, and said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me.
verses.little_bible: After saying this, Jesus felt deeply troubled inside. Then He said these solemn words: 'I tell you the truth — one of you sitting here will betray Me.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus felt very sad inside. He said: 'One of you will betray Me.'
verses.meaning: Jesus was not distant from the pain of betrayal. He felt it — deeply. God is not a cold, unmoved God. He is moved by sadness, by love, by the cost of our sin.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for feeling pain for my sake.
verses.discussion_question: Has a friend ever let you down? How did it feel?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus was 'troubled in spirit' — deeply sorrowful. Knowing that Jesus feels pain helps us understand that He fully understands our pain. How does that comfort you?
verses.do_it_today: If you have hurt a friend, go and say sorry today — don't let the pain go on.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus looking troubled and deeply sad, His hands pressed together, the disciples looking at each other in alarm and confusion, the mood in the room suddenly heavy. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Then the disciples looked one on another, doubting of whom he spake.
verses.little_bible: The disciples looked at each other, confused and worried. They had no idea who Jesus was talking about.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The disciples looked at each other. Who could it be?
verses.meaning: Nobody immediately pointed to Judas. The disciples questioned themselves first. This should be a reminder to examine our own hearts honestly before pointing fingers at others.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, search my heart for anything wrong.
verses.discussion_question: When something goes wrong, do you quickly blame others or look at yourself first?
verses.family_discussion: The disciples looked at each other wondering if it was themselves. How can we make a habit of honest self-examination before God?
verses.do_it_today: Spend one quiet minute asking God: 'Is there something wrong in my heart right now?'
verses.illustration_prompt: The disciples at the table looking at each other with wide, worried eyes, pointing at themselves and at each other in confusion, the air tense and uncertain. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Now there was leaning on Jesus' bosom one of his disciples, whom Jesus loved.
verses.little_bible: One of the disciples was sitting very close to Jesus, leaning right next to Him. This was the disciple Jesus especially loved.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: One disciple sat very close to Jesus — the one Jesus loved dearly.
verses.meaning: The 'disciple whom Jesus loved' is John himself, writing his own Gospel. He was close enough to lean on Jesus. We too are invited to come close to Jesus — to rest near His heart.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, I want to stay close to Your heart always.
verses.discussion_question: What does it feel like to be close to someone who loves you?
verses.family_discussion: John was very close to Jesus at the table. How can you draw closer to Jesus in your daily life?
verses.do_it_today: Spend five extra minutes with Jesus today — reading, praying, or just being still.
verses.illustration_prompt: A young disciple leaning gently against Jesus at the table, eyes closed in peace, Jesus's arm around him warmly, the meal spread before them, soft golden lamplight. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Simon Peter therefore beckoned to him, that he should ask who it should be of whom he spake.
verses.little_bible: Simon Peter caught the attention of the disciple close to Jesus. He motioned to him: 'Ask Jesus who it is He is talking about!'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Peter quietly motioned to the disciple: 'Ask Jesus who it is!'
verses.meaning: Peter wanted to know, but instead of asking directly, he asked the one closest to Jesus. The closer we are to Jesus, the better placed we are to hear from Him on behalf of others.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, draw me close so I can hear Your voice clearly.
verses.discussion_question: Why do you think Peter asked someone else to ask Jesus instead of asking himself?
verses.family_discussion: The disciple closest to Jesus was the one who could most easily get an answer. How does spending time close to Jesus help us hear from God?
verses.do_it_today: Pray and ask Jesus something you genuinely want to know — then listen.
verses.illustration_prompt: Peter at the far end of the table catching the eye of the beloved disciple, gesturing urgently but quietly toward Jesus, the beloved disciple nodding. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: He then lying on Jesus' breast saith unto him, Lord, who is it?
verses.little_bible: The beloved disciple leaned even closer to Jesus and quietly asked: 'Lord, who is it?'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The disciple leaned close and whispered: 'Lord, who is it?'
verses.meaning: A whispered question, asked in closeness. The most personal moments with Jesus happen when we get close and simply ask Him. He answers those who come near.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me be honest with You and ask what I need to ask.
verses.discussion_question: Is there something you have been wanting to ask Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: The disciple leaned close and asked Jesus honestly. Is there a question your family can bring honestly to Jesus in prayer right now?
verses.do_it_today: Write down one honest question for Jesus and pray it — then look for His answer in Scripture.
verses.illustration_prompt: The beloved disciple leaning very close to Jesus, whispering quietly, Jesus bending slightly to hear, an intimate and quiet scene amid the larger table gathering. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Jesus answered, He it is, to whom I shall give a sop, when I have dipped it. And when he had dipped the sop, he gave it to Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon.
verses.little_bible: Jesus answered: 'The one I give this piece of bread to — that is the one.' Then He dipped a piece of bread and gave it to Judas Iscariot.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus dipped a piece of bread and gave it to Judas. That was the sign.
verses.meaning: Even in revealing the betrayer, Jesus acted with dignity. Giving someone a piece of dipped bread was a gesture of honour. Jesus extended grace to Judas right to the very end.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me show kindness even to those who hurt me.
verses.discussion_question: Is it easy or hard to be kind to someone who is being unkind to you?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus gave Judas a gesture of honour even knowing he would betray Him. How can showing kindness to difficult people reflect the love of Jesus?
verses.do_it_today: Show unexpected kindness to someone who has been difficult — give them something or say something kind.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus holding out a piece of dipped bread to Judas across the table, Judas reaching to take it, the moment heavy with significance, the other disciples unaware of what it means. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: And after the sop Satan entered into him. Then said Jesus unto him, That thou doest, do quickly.
verses.little_bible: As soon as Judas took the bread, Satan entered into him. Jesus said to Judas: 'Whatever you are going to do — do it quickly.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Satan entered Judas. Jesus said: 'Do it quickly.'
verses.meaning: Judas made his final choice. Once we fully reject Jesus and give ourselves to evil, we open the door to something far darker. Jesus, in full control, told him to proceed — because even this was within God's plan.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, protect me from the enemy and keep me close to You.
verses.discussion_question: Who is stronger — Satan or Jesus? How do you know?
verses.family_discussion: Even when Satan entered Judas, Jesus was in control. How does knowing that Jesus is more powerful than Satan give you confidence and peace?
verses.do_it_today: Pray a short prayer today asking Jesus to protect your mind and heart from evil.
verses.illustration_prompt: Judas standing up from the table, a dark shadow over his face, Jesus watching him calmly and without fear, the other disciples confused, the door of the room ahead. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Now no man at the table knew for what intent he spake this unto him.
verses.little_bible: None of the other disciples understood why Jesus had said that to Judas.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: No one else at the table understood what Jesus meant.
verses.meaning: God's deepest plans are often hidden from those around us. The disciples were watching the same moment but could not see what was happening. Faith trusts God even when we cannot see clearly.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, I trust You even when I cannot see clearly.
verses.discussion_question: Can you still trust someone even if you don't understand everything they do?
verses.family_discussion: The disciples didn't understand what was happening — but God did. How does trusting that God sees everything help us when we are confused?
verses.do_it_today: Think of something confusing in your life right now. Say: 'God, I trust You with this even though I don't understand it.'
verses.illustration_prompt: The disciples around the table with puzzled expressions, looking at the door where Judas has gone, Jesus sitting quietly with a calm but serious face. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: For some of them thought, because Judas had the bag, that Jesus had said unto him, Buy those things that we have need of against the feast; or, that he should give something to the poor.
verses.little_bible: Some disciples thought Jesus had told Judas to go and buy things for the feast — because Judas looked after the group's money. Or maybe he was going to give to the poor.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Some thought Judas went to buy food or give to the poor — they had no idea.
verses.meaning: Giving to the poor was such a normal part of their life with Jesus that it seemed a natural guess. What a powerful picture: even at the most dramatic moment of history, caring for the poor was simply assumed.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help my family always remember the poor.
verses.discussion_question: Do you think about giving to people who are poor? How could you help?
verses.family_discussion: Giving to the poor was so normal in Jesus's group that the disciples assumed that might be why Judas left. How central is generosity to your family's life?
verses.do_it_today: Find something you can give away this week — money, food, clothes, or time — and give it to someone in need.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two disciples at the table whispering to each other, one miming buying at a market, the other gesturing toward the poor, both looking unbothered, Judas already gone. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: He then having received the sop went immediately out: and it was night.
verses.little_bible: As soon as Judas took the bread, he walked straight out the door. And it was night.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Judas went out immediately. It was night.
verses.meaning: John records one devastating detail: it was night. In John's Gospel, night is a symbol of darkness and evil. Judas walked out of the light of Jesus — into the dark. Every step away from Jesus is a step into darkness.
verses.memory_phrase: Stay in the light of Jesus.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, keep me in Your light — never let me walk away.
verses.discussion_question: What happens when you go from a bright light into a very dark room?
verses.family_discussion: Judas went from sitting at the table with Jesus into the night. What does this image of light and darkness teach us about staying close to Jesus?
verses.do_it_today: Light a candle or a lamp tonight and pray together as a family. Thank Jesus for being your light.
verses.illustration_prompt: The door of the upper room open to a dark night sky, Judas's silhouette walking out alone, the warm light of the room behind him, the contrast stark and sad. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Therefore, when he was gone out, Jesus said, Now is the Son of man glorified, and God is glorified in him.
verses.little_bible: Once Judas had gone, Jesus said: 'Now the Son of Man is glorified — and God is glorified in Him.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: When Judas left, Jesus said: 'Now God will be glorified!'
verses.meaning: Now the path to the cross was open. Jesus saw what was coming not as defeat but as glory. The cross is where God's love, justice, and power would all be displayed at once.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, let Your glory be shown in my life too.
verses.discussion_question: How can something that looks like a sad ending actually be a glorious beginning?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus called the cross His glory. How does the cross show us what God's glory really looks like — not power and riches, but love and sacrifice?
verses.do_it_today: Think of a hard thing in your life and ask: 'How might God be glorified through this?'
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus standing tall and speaking with a look of quiet triumph and peace, the upper room filled with warm golden light, the disciples watching in awe. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: If God be glorified in him, God shall also glorify him in himself, and shall straightway glorify him.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'If God is glorified in the Son, then God will also glorify the Son — and will do it very soon.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'God will glorify Me — and soon!'
verses.meaning: Jesus speaks of His resurrection and exaltation — the honour that would come after the cross. The Father does not leave His Son in suffering. After the cross comes the resurrection, the ascension, the glory.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for the glory that came after Your suffering.
verses.discussion_question: Can you think of a time when something hard led to something wonderful?
verses.family_discussion: God glorified Jesus after the cross. How does knowing that our sufferings are not the end of the story change the way we face hard times?
verses.do_it_today: Write: 'This hard time is not the end of the story.' Put it somewhere you can see it.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus looking upward with peace and certainty on His face, a faint glow surrounding Him, the disciples watching as if catching a glimpse of something magnificent. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Little children, yet a little while I am with you. Ye shall seek me: and as I said unto the Jews, Whither I go, ye cannot come; so now I say to you.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said tenderly: 'My dear children, I am only with you a little while longer. You will look for Me — but where I am going, you cannot come yet.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'I can only stay a little longer. Where I go, you cannot come yet.'
verses.meaning: Jesus called His disciples 'little children' — a term of the deepest tenderness. His departure was not abandonment. He was going to prepare a place, and He would call them home in time.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for calling me Your child.
verses.discussion_question: How does it feel when someone you love has to go away for a while?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus calls His disciples 'little children.' What does it mean to you that Jesus sees us as His beloved children?
verses.do_it_today: Say out loud three times: 'I am a child of Jesus.' Thank Him for that truth.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus leaning forward tenderly at the table, hands extended toward the disciples as if embracing them with His words, the disciples' faces soft with love and sadness. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'I give you a new command: love one another. Love each other the same way I have loved you.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'Love one another — just like I love you.'
verses.meaning: This is Jesus's new commandment — the defining mark of His followers. Not love as the world loves, but love as Jesus loves: self-giving, serving, sacrificial. This is the highest standard of love.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me love others the way You love me.
verses.discussion_question: How does Jesus love us? Can you love someone that way today?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus made love for one another a commandment — not a suggestion. What would your family look like if you loved each other exactly the way Jesus loves you?
verses.do_it_today: Choose one person and love them today the way Jesus loves — patiently, kindly, without keeping score.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus with both hands on His heart and arms outstretched toward the disciples, a radiant expression of love and urgency, the disciples moved and leaning forward. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'Everyone will know you are My disciples by one thing — if you love one another.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'People will know you follow Me if you love each other.'
verses.meaning: Love is the badge of a Christian. Not a church building, not a label, not a tradition — but love. The world should be able to look at Christians and say: 'See how they love one another.'
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, let my love show the world that I belong to You.
verses.discussion_question: How can people tell that you belong to Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus says love is how people will know we are His disciples. How are you doing? Can others see the love of Jesus in your family?
verses.do_it_today: Do one loving thing in public today — and let it be your testimony.
verses.illustration_prompt: A small group of disciples walking together through a busy street, people around them watching and pointing, the disciples sharing bread, helping a stranger, smiling — a visible community of love. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Simon Peter said unto him, Lord, whither goest thou? Jesus answered him, Whither I go, thou canst not follow me now; but thou shalt follow me afterwards.
verses.little_bible: Peter asked: 'Lord, where are You going?' Jesus answered: 'You cannot follow Me there now — but you will follow Me later.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Peter asked: 'Where are You going?' Jesus said: 'Not now. But you will follow later.'
verses.meaning: Peter's question was bold and loving — he could not bear the thought of Jesus leaving. Jesus's answer was gentle: 'not yet, but one day.' There is a place Jesus has gone to prepare for all who follow Him.
verses.memory_phrase: We will follow Jesus one day.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, I want to follow You all my life and one day be with You.
verses.discussion_question: Where do you think Jesus went when He left the earth?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus said Peter would follow Him later. For Christians, this points to heaven. What do you think it will be like to follow Jesus all the way to where He is?
verses.do_it_today: Talk with your family about what you are looking forward to about being with Jesus one day.
verses.illustration_prompt: Peter leaning urgently toward Jesus, eyes wide with longing, Jesus answering with patient love, pointing upward with one hand, the door of the room visible behind Him. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Peter said unto him, Lord, why cannot I follow thee now? I will lay down my life for thy sake.
verses.little_bible: Peter said: 'Lord, why can't I follow You now? I will give my life for You!'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Peter said: 'Why not now? I would die for You, Lord!'
verses.meaning: Peter meant every word — and later he did die for Jesus. But in this moment, he did not know his own weakness. It is good to be brave and willing, but we must also be honest about how much we need Jesus's strength.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, make me brave and keep me humble before You.
verses.discussion_question: Have you ever promised something big and found it was harder than you thought?
verses.family_discussion: Peter was very brave and very sincere — but he overestimated himself. How can we be willing to follow Jesus while also knowing we need His help to do it?
verses.do_it_today: Make a brave promise to Jesus today — and then ask Him to help you keep it.
verses.illustration_prompt: Peter standing up at the table with one hand on his chest, eyes passionate and full of devotion, Jesus looking at him with deep love and gentle knowing sadness. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Jesus answered him, Wilt thou lay down thy life for my sake? Verily, verily, I say unto thee, The cock shall not crow, till thou hast denied me thrice.
verses.little_bible: Jesus answered: 'Will you really give your life for Me? I tell you the truth — before the rooster crows, you will say three times that you don't know Me.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'Before the rooster crows, you will say three times you don't know Me.'
verses.meaning: Jesus was not mocking Peter — He was warning him. He knew Peter's heart better than Peter did. And yet Jesus did not reject him. He already planned to restore Peter after his failure. Jesus knows our weaknesses and loves us still.
verses.memory_phrase: Jesus loves us in our weakness.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, when I fail You, please restore me like You restored Peter.
verses.discussion_question: If you made a big mistake, would you come back to Jesus? Why?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus told Peter he would fail — but Jesus never stopped loving Peter. Has God ever loved you through a failure? What happened?
verses.do_it_today: If there is a way you have failed Jesus recently, tell Him right now. He already knows — and He already loves you.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus looking at Peter with solemn, knowing, tender eyes, Peter's expression falling as the words sink in, a rooster perched faintly visible outside the window in the night, warm room around them. Storybook watercolour.
